key_insight: JEFFNet combines self-supervised JEPA features with EfficientNetV2-S convolutional features to improve thermal IR-based solar PV fault classification while keeping the model more parameter-efficient.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable, non-contact inspection method that can help automate fault detection for large photovoltaic installations.
method: Pretrain a Vision Transformer with JEPA on thermal IR images to learn semantic representations without labels.
Extract supervised convolutional features using EfficientNetV2-S.
Fuse both feature streams in a multibranch JEFFNet classifier for multiclass and healthy/faulty detection.
evidence_signal: On PVF-10 and ISM, JEFFNet achieved strong performance in both multiclass and binary tasks, including 94.33% accuracy on PVF-10 (10-class) and 94.78% accuracy on ISM (2-class), while using 108.6M parameters.
watch_item: Performance is still dataset-dependent and the lower multiclass score on ISM suggests class imbalance and subtle thermal distinctions remain challenging.
paper_title: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Solar PV Panel Fault Classification
